date.as_written: śāke 1688 saṃvat 1823 durmukhanāma samvatsare māsottame māse śrāvaṇamāse kṛṣṇapakṣe 2 vudhavāratādina

notes: The colophon gives two eras, ŚS 1688 and VS 1823. They agree: both give 1766 CE. The year name Durmukha would fit a northern (bārhaspatya) reckoning of the 60-year cycle and has not been checked exactly; the southern cycle would give Vyaya. The scribe's name 'narāpapādasa' is probably corrupt; it may stand for Nārāyaṇadāsa or Narapatidāsa. 'bhārgava vrāhmaṇa' marks him as a Bhārgava brahmin. 'sāḍhoṃre vāre' is Hindi for 'from Sāḍhaurā' (probably Sadhaura, Yamunanagar district, Haryana). 'kasavāranodamadhye' probably means 'in the kasbā (town) of Ranod' (perhaps Ranod, Shivpuri district, Madhya Pradesh), but this is uncertain. This is a north Indian (not Nepalese) manuscript.
